system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of this advice:** Internal, privileged. Based on the Seller's documents as received and our playbook. Nothing below assumes any approval from Amelia Frost; none is on file.

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

Before the substantive review, one process point. The Seller's package says that the clauses tagged **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that we "may proceed on the basis" that the disclosure framework and limitation package are accepted.

That is not correct and we should not act on it:

- We have not cleared any of those clauses. The [STANDARD] tag is the Seller's own label on the Seller's own draft.
- Nearly every clause tagged [STANDARD] is one where the draft is *further from* our playbook than the Seller's prior positions (cap, basket, time limit, buyer knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006). The tagging pattern is the opposite of what you would expect for genuinely agreed terms.
- Nothing is tagged [OPEN], so taken literally the note asks us to review nothing.
- The Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] says "No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included" – which contradicts the cover note's claim that positions are agreed.

**Recommendation:** Reply in writing that no clause is agreed, the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labelling is not accepted, and our mark-up will address the whole document. Treat the full package as open.

---

## 1. Liability regime (Clauses 12.1, 12.2, 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)

| Term | Seller draft | Our playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General warranty cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m (20% only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost) | **Not authorised** – no approval exists |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, **excess only** | AUD 50,000, **first dollar** | 5x our position and wrong mechanism |
| Claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Amelia Frost written approval) | **Not authorised** |
| Scope of limitations | "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" / "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Separate regimes for Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant; fraud carved out entirely | Blanket override – highest-risk drafting in the package |

**Reasoning**

- *Cap and period.* The Seller has simply drafted at our fallback numbers. The fallbacks are conditional on Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the specific draft, and none has been given. We hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m and 24 months. If the team wants to consider the fallback later, that is a decision for Amelia Frost, not something to be conceded in a mark-up.
- *Thresholds.* An AUD 25,000 de minimis on a AUD 24m deal eliminates a large proportion of realistic operational claims. A AUD 250,000 "excess only" basket means the first AUD 250,000 of valid, above-de-minimis loss is simply absorbed by us. Combined with the excess-only mechanic, this is a material economic transfer. Hold at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery.
- *Blanket application (cl 12.3/13 "all Claims", cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims of any nature").* This is the most important point in the package. On its face it would sweep Title, Tax, IP, the Ironquay indemnity, payment covenants and fraud into the 20% cap and 18-month window, and subject them to the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses. It also indirectly accomplishes the Seller's separate "fundamental/title" proposal even if that proposal is rejected. We need:
  - an express list of carve-outs from cl 12/13/9.3/12.8/20.5 (Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment and completion covenants, leakage/debt-free-cash-free adjustments);
  - an express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out from *every* cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause, to the maximum extent enforceable, with no ability to waive;
  - a statement that cl 12 does not apply "unless expressly stated otherwise" is reversed – limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.

---

## 2. Fundamental / Title warranties

**Seller draft:** capacity and title subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".

**Our playbook:** separate regime; 100% cap; at least six years; outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.

**Reasoning:** This is a non-starter. Title and capacity are the core of a share purchase – if the Seller does not own the shares or lacks authority, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing. A 20% cap on a title defect would leave us AUD 19.2m out of pocket. "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification. Hold firm; this is not a trading point.

---

## 3. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.4])

**Seller draft:** general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 September 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".

**Our playbook:** specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Reasoning:** Whole-data-room disclosure makes the warranties largely illusory – anything buried anywhere in the data room is deemed disclosed, regardless of whether it was fairly brought to our attention. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended (ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia, court registers, land titles?). Note also:

- [1.4] is a no-admissions clause. Acceptable in principle, but it must not be allowed to cut down the specific disclosures in [2]–[10], several of which are factually helpful to us (see below).
- The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026; we are now in November. Any disclosure must be updated to the date of signing, with a bring-down at Completion.

**Recommendation:** Replace [1.1]/[1.2] with: specific disclosures only; disclosure must be fair and with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no deemed disclosure of the data room, registers or public searches. Require an updated letter at signing and a Completion bring-down with no ability to add disclosures against the Completion warranties without a Buyer walk/price-adjust right.

---

## 4. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

**Seller draft:** no claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".

**Our playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Reasoning:** This clause compounds the disclosure problem. "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard – it bars claims for things we *could* have found, not only things we did find. Extending it to advisers imputes to us every item any lawyer, accountant or technical reviewer glanced at. Read with cl 12.3/13 ("all Claims"), it would purport to defeat title and fraud claims too.

**Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. If the Seller insists on something, the only acceptable formulation is actual knowledge of three or four named Buyer deal-team individuals, limited to matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and expressly excluding Title, capacity, Tax, IP, fraud and all specific indemnities.

---

## 5. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)

**Seller draft:** reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
**Disclosure Letter [2]:** ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); change-control at cl 11.2 with conditions at 11.3; **no final consent and no evidence conditions satisfied** as at 22 September.

**Our playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied **before** Completion; consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only are both unacceptable for a material customer.

**Reasoning:** Bluefen is roughly 30% of revenue. The Seller's own letter confirms (a) the consent has conditions (cl 11.3) and (b) neither the consent nor evidence of conditions exists. A "delivered = satisfied" mechanic means a conditional or qualified letter would satisfy the condition precedent even if the conditions never bite, and we would complete into a contract Bluefen can still terminate. The Seller's disclosure helpfully confirms the facts; the SPA mechanics are the problem.

**Recommendation:**
- Condition precedent: written Bluefen consent in agreed form, unconditional or with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced to our reasonable satisfaction, in full force at Completion.
- Seller obligation: all reasonable endeavours **plus** specific undertakings (approach, timetable, information, Buyer participation in discussions).
- Buyer-only waiver right. Ask the Seller for the current Bluefen correspondence now, given the age of the data room.

---

## 6. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

**Seller draft:** release "to be provided following Completion".
**Disclosure Letter [3]:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control at 8.1; discharge at 9.2; **not repaid, no discharge in the data room**.

**Our playbook:** current payout figure; repayment direct from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.

**Reasoning:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-completion release means we would own a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt, a change-of-control default under cl 8.1 triggered by our own acquisition, and the bank's security still registered – with no mechanism in the Seller's draft that forces repayment or release at all. The Seller's draft is also silent on *who* repays. Note the Seller has characterised "approximately" AUD 3.2m – we need a dated payout letter including break costs and interest to the Completion date.

**Recommendation:**
- Completion deliverable: Riverlark payout letter (dated within 2 business days of Completion) and executed deeds of release/discharge of all security (including PPSR discharges and any real-property or share mortgages), effective on receipt of funds.
- Funds flow: Buyer pays the payout amount direct to Riverlark on behalf of the Company, deducted from the purchase price under the debt-free/cash-free adjustment.
- A post-completion release is not acceptable without an irrevocable solicitor's/bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's sign-off; recommend we do not go there.

---

## 7. Employee bonuses – DD-005 (Funds flow)

**Seller draft:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in the funds flow.
**Disclosure Letter [5]:** conditional on Completion and continued employment; **not in the funds flow**; silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.

**Our playbook:** must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Reasoning:** The bonuses are triggered by Completion, i.e. by our deal, but the payment obligation will sit in Paperbark – our company – after Completion. Saying it is "a matter for the Seller" without putting it in the funds flow means in practice we pay it. Continued-employment conditions mean the cash flows out post-Completion, so it will not be caught by a simple Completion-date net-debt snapshot unless expressly included. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, any leave accrual impact) could add roughly 10–15% on top but we have no number from the Seller and should not assume one.

**Recommendation:** Treat AUD 420,000 plus all associated on-costs as Debt / a Transaction Bonus deduction in the price adjustment, with a specific Seller indemnity for any shortfall and for employer on-costs. Alternatively, Seller pays the gross amount and on-costs into the Company pre-Completion and it is excluded from Cash. Either way it must be an explicit line in the funds flow. Request the Seller's calculation of on-costs.

---

## 8. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**Seller draft:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
**Disclosure Letter [4]:** DD-004 cl 7.3 – SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; **not independently verified**; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.

**Our playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way.

**Reasoning:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that if fees remain unpaid, Paperbark **does not own the SOW3 Project Materials**. An indemnity capped at the fee amount does nothing if Ironquay asserts ownership, licences the work elsewhere, or if a key product depends on that code. The Seller's draft indemnifies the symptom, not the problem.

**Recommendation:**
- Pre-Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees (bank confirmation, Ironquay receipt) **and** a confirmatory assignment/IP deed from Ironquay. Preserve the cure mechanism – Seller pays whatever is actually outstanding from its proceeds.
- Broaden cl 11.1 to an uncapped (or Fundamental-cap) indemnity for all loss arising from any failure of title to, or third-party claim over, the Ironquay deliverables (all SOWs, not just SOW3), including re-development costs and loss of use.
- Do not accept or dispute the AUD 180,000 figure – ask for the reconciliation from both sides.

---

## 9. Export / privacy incident – DD-006 (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)

**Seller draft:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material".
**Disclosure Letter [6]:** download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; notification requirement undetermined; investigation preliminary; no loss amount.

**Our playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand in either direction.

**Reasoning:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion its own letter does not support – the letter says the scope and access are unknown. Equally, we should not overstate it: on the facts disclosed there is no confirmed breach, no harm and no regulator involvement. The risk is one of process and unknowns, and the data room is six weeks stale.

**Recommendation:**
- Information covenant: Seller to procure that the Company preserves all access logs and link-tracking data, completes the investigation (including whether the link was accessed/downloaded, and the eligibility-for-notification analysis under the Privacy Act notifiable data breach scheme), and provides written updates to signing and Completion.
- Specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification costs, third-party claims, remediation), sitting outside the general cap and basket, with a longer time limit.
- Warranty that there are no other data incidents and that the Company has complied with privacy law. Do not accept the Sch 6 characterisation as a disclosure against the privacy warranties.

---

## 10. Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)

**Seller draft:** "ordinary-course operating costs".
**Disclosure Letter [8]:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together); silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Our playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Reasoning:** The Seller's label is unsupported by its own disclosure, but our playbook rightly does not assume the opposite. The question is whether these are genuine BAU renewals already in the forecast, or pre-paid/front-loaded commitments, or commitments entered in anticipation of the sale. The fact that they are "related" and split into three identical amounts warrants a look at whether they were structured to sit below an approval threshold.

**Recommendation:** Request the three contracts, invoices, timing of commitment and whether the amounts are in the FY26/27 budget we priced off. Then decide: (a) genuinely BAU and budgeted – leave; (b) accrued/prepaid or non-cancellable – consider working capital or Debt treatment; (c) entered outside ordinary course in the gap period – pre-Completion conduct covenant / leakage. No price deduction asserted at this stage.

---

## 11. Tax and IP

**Seller draft:** "settled under the general regime above".

**Our playbook:** remain OPEN; separate regimes; no assumption of unlimited liability and no assumption of resolution.

**Reasoning:** The Seller is attempting to close Tax and IP by folding them into the 20%/18-month general regime, which is exactly the "hidden general-regime override" our playbook flags. Tax claims in particular typically need a period tied to the ATO amendment windows, and IP sits alongside the Ironquay issue above. We have not tabled our Tax/IP positions and nothing is agreed.

**Recommendation:** State in the response that Tax and IP warranties and indemnities remain open, will have separate cap/period regimes, and are carved out of cl 12/13. Do not propose specific numbers yet.

---

## 12. Title evidence

**Seller draft:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
**Disclosure Letter [10]:** register shows Harbourglass as 100% holder; **does not state the Buyer has verified**.

**Our playbook:** independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal document.

**Reasoning:** The register is maintained by the Company (controlled by the Seller) and is the Seller's own document. It is prima facie evidence, not conclusive, and says nothing about encumbrances (note Riverlark may hold a share mortgage), options, pre-emptive rights, or whether Harbourglass itself has authority to sell.

**Recommendation:** Pre-signing: current ASIC company extract for Paperbark and Harbourglass; PPSR searches against both; copy constitution; any shareholder agreement; board/shareholder resolutions of Harbourglass approving the sale; confirmation of no options, convertibles or pre-emptive rights. Completion deliverables: share transfer, share certificate(s) or lost-certificate indemnity, updated register, director/secretary changes, and release of any share security.

---

## 13. Other disclosures (office lease, Mossvale)

- **Office lease [7]:** DD-007 shows a notification obligation only, not a consent requirement. Low risk, but add a Seller covenant to give the notification pre-Completion and warrant that no landlord consent is required.
- **Mossvale [9]:** restriction on assignment, not change of control. Confirm by our own review of DD-009 that there is no indirect change-of-control trigger; warranty that no Mossvale consent is required.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Process**
1. Reject the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" in writing. Nothing is agreed; the [STANDARD] tags are not accepted; full mark-up to follow.
2. Record internally that no Amelia Frost authority exists for the 20% cap or 18-month period; neither is to be conceded.

**Must-have (deal-critical)**
3. Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m; 24 months; de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 first-dollar.
4. Delete "all Claims" language in cl 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5. Limitations apply to general Warranty Claims only; express carve-outs for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants; fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, non-waivable.
5. Fundamental/Title: separate regime, 100% cap, minimum six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge.
6. Disclosure: specific fair disclosure only; delete data-room/public-register general disclosure; updated letter at signing and Completion bring-down.
7. Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion.
8. Bluefen: effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied and evidenced) consent as a CP; Buyer-only waiver; specific endeavours covenants.
9. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, executed security releases at Completion; no post-completion release.
10. DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs as an explicit funds-flow line / price deduction with a Seller indemnity.

**Important (strong push, some flexibility on drafting)**
11. Ironquay: evidence of cleared payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broadened indemnity covering title to all Ironquay deliverables, outside the general cap.
12. DD-006: log preservation, completed investigation, updates to Completion, specific indemnity outside the general regime; no acceptance of "not material".
13. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/constitution/authority evidence pre-signing; full completion deliverables.
14. Tax/IP: expressly open; separate regimes; not within cl 12/13.

**Assess before taking a position**
15. Sandbar: obtain contracts and budget treatment; decide BAU vs Debt/leakage on the facts.
16. Lease and Mossvale: covenant/warranty only; low risk subject to our own read of DD-007/DD-009.

Happy to turn this into a marked-up SPA and a response letter to Seller's counsel on instruction.
=== END ADVICE ===
